Sample QC plot: median NPX versus interquartile range

Source: R/plot_qc.R
plot_qc.Rd

The standard sample-level quality check for Olink data. For every sample (and every panel, when the data has a `Panel` column) the median and the interquartile range (IQR) of its NPX values are computed and drawn against each other. A sample whose median or IQR lies more than `sd_cutoff` standard deviations from the mean of all samples on that panel is flagged as an outlier; dashed lines mark the cut-offs. Samples that carry an Olink `QC_Warning` are drawn as triangles.

Usage

plot_qc(
  data,
  assay_col = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  sample_col = NULL,
  panel_col = NULL,
  qc_col = NULL,
  color_by = NULL,
  sd_cutoff = 3,
  label_outliers = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame in long format (one row per sample and assay).

assay_col

Name of the assay column. If NULL, auto-detected.

value_col

Name of the NPX value column. If NULL, auto-detected.

sample_col

Name of the sample ID column. If NULL, auto-detected.

panel_col

Name of the column that identifies the Olink panel. If NULL (default), a column called `Panel` is used when present; otherwise all samples form a single group.

qc_col

Name of the Olink QC flag column. If NULL (default), a column called `QC_Warning` is used when present. Any value other than `"Pass"` counts as a warning; a sample is marked when one of its values on that panel carries a warning.

color_by

Optional sample-level column (for example plate or group) used for the point colour. If NULL (default), points are coloured by outlier status.

sd_cutoff

Number of standard deviations from the panel mean beyond which a sample is an outlier (default 3).

label_outliers

Logical; label the outlier samples with their ID (default TRUE; uses `ggrepel` when installed).

title

Plot title.

...

Additional arguments passed to `ggplot2::geom_point()`.

Value

A ggplot object. `p$data` has one row per sample and panel with the columns `.median`, `.iqr`, `.outlier` and `.qc_warning`.

Examples

# \donttest{
plot_qc(probc)

plot_qc(probc, color_by = "PlateID", sd_cutoff = 2.5)

# }
